formula: So + auxiliary + subject (So do I) · Neither/Nor + auxiliary + subject · one/ones for nouns · do so / do the same for verb phrases · omission of repeated words (I'd like to, but I can't)
formula_visual: [So] + [do] + [I] · I'd like to come, but I can't [come]
when_to_use: To avoid repetition, which English strongly prefers. 'So do I' agrees positively; 'Neither do I' agrees negatively; 'one/ones' replaces a repeated noun; 'do so' replaces a whole verb phrase in formal contexts; and repeated words are simply deleted after an auxiliary ('I can't'). Using ellipsis well is one of the clearest markers of natural, fluent English.
when_to_use_ar: لتجنّب التكرار الذي تكرهه الإنجليزية. 'So do I' للموافقة المثبتة، و'Neither do I' للمنفية، و'one/ones' لاستبدال الاسم، و'do so' لعبارة فعلية كاملة في السياق الرسمي.
why_arabic_speakers_struggle: Arabic tolerates repetition comfortably and marks agreement with pronoun-plus-particle constructions (وأنا أيضًا), so there is no pressure to compress and no inversion involved. Learners therefore repeat the full verb, which sounds laboured, or they produce 'So I do' without inverting. The negative pattern causes a further error: because 'neither' already carries the negative, adding another one ('Neither I don't') reverses the meaning.

examples.en: I love this city. — So do I.
I don't agree. — Neither do I.
I'll take the cheaper ones, thanks.
She was asked to explain and did so willingly.
examples.ar: طُلب منها أن تشرح ففعلت ذلك برضا

examples.en: I'd like to come, but I can't.
examples.ar: أودّ أن آتي، لكن لا أستطيع

common_errors.explanation: After 'so' and 'neither' the auxiliary comes before the subject.
'Neither' already carries the negative, so a second one reverses the meaning.
The plural of the substitute is 'ones' with no apostrophe.

common_errors.wrong: She was asked to explain and did so it.
common_errors.correct: She was asked to explain and did so.
common_errors.explanation: 'Do so' already replaces the whole verb phrase, so no object is added.

practice_fill_blank.sentence: Anyone wishing to object may do ___ in writing.

quick_rule: So/Neither + auxiliary + subject (invert!). One negative only. one/ones for nouns, do so for verb phrases.
quick_rule_ar: So/Neither + المساعد + الفاعل (اقلب!). ونفي واحد فقط. وone/ones للأسماء، وdo so للعبارات الفعلية.
mnemonic: Say it once, then let an auxiliary carry the rest.
connect_to_speaking: In accent week 11 you drilled the strong substituting auxiliary: 'So DO I'. Because that one word replaces a whole clause, it must be stressed — said flatly it sounds oddly uncommitted.
